title: A Love Stronger Than Heaven or Hell
note: Adapted from author's Parts Four–Six; dialogue lightly copyedited; narration condensed. Joren is identified by author as gang boss even though story manuscript calls him 'youth' or 'gang leader'.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Cool water touched Haniel's lips and coaxed her awake. Asmodeus knelt beside her, holding a particularly large seashell to her mouth.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: His eyes widened when he realized she was awake. Her body still ached from the fight with the bear.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Hey.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Why?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She tilted her head, drinking from the seashell.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I told you the strong's duty is to do as they please with the weak. That bear had me at its mercy. Yet despite disagreeing with my worldview, you still saved my ass yesterday... why?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He sounded soft and genuinely confused. Haniel began to wonder whether this demon was different from the others she'd known.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Then, as the one who defeated it, it was my right to save you and to take its life, given your own philosophy.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She signed slowly with heavy, clumsy hands. She remembered the fear the bear had felt when she killed it.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Just don't let its body be wasted. All the beasts of the land deserve that respect, at least.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus smiled, showing his sharp teeth.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I figured you'd say something cliche like that.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She felt both indignant and strangely warm at his chuckle.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Don't look at me with that expression. I turned its fur into a blanket, the very one you are laying on.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel finally noticed the bear-fur blanket. Had he done it for her, or did he appreciate life in his own way?

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Thank you.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Nah, I should be the one kissing your ass. You saved my life, not even a week after we tried killing each other, and I'm sure your bosses wouldn't be thrilled knowing you saved the prince of lust.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: His grin faded as he looked away.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Then we both owe thanks, so none needs to be given.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel smiled. Asmodeus smiled back.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus surveyed the grassy clearing he'd made outside the cave. Haniel sat on the ledge behind him, still recovering.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Damnit.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The crude rack he'd built for drying hides collapsed again. He was accustomed to servants who handled all the mundane work.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: But servants were boring. Haniel wasn't. She challenged him—and that made him feel alive in a way he hadn't since the rings were conquered.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Luci can wait a few more days, or weeks, or whatever.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel tilted her head. Asmodeus knew this comfortable life would eventually end, and that they'd return to their respective peoples as enemies.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Do you miss it?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel climbed down from the ledge. She mulled his question over like a puzzle.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Yes.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Yet her eyes didn't sparkle as they did when rabbits grazed nearby or when the sunrise touched the forest.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: What about that place is so great?

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: It's home.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus didn't believe she would ever fall. He'd met fallen angels before, and none was anything like her.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Whatever, let's just eat or whatever.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He turned to their charcoal-filled firepit. If he had to play house with an angel, he was glad it was this one.

events.title: THE NATURE OF MAN AND DEMONS

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel felt heavy and tired as they entered the human town nearest their camp. Its dirt roads were busier than anything she'd imagined.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Cliffside. What weird namers humans are.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: If I was in charge of naming towns they would be named something scarier to frighten off the possibility of attacks. Something like Bloodfell, or Life's Bane, not named because of its placement upon the earth.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: His complaints sounded annoyed, but Haniel could feel that he enjoyed them.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: They approached a shop with baskets of merchandise near the front door.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Stay here.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He pointed to a crate. Haniel sat, rolling her eyes as he went inside. Her halo was warm within her bag; without it she felt vulnerable.

events.speaker: BLOND YOUTH
events.text: Hey, miss, could ya come and give my friend some help? He's hurt pretty bad.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A skinny blond man with shoulder-length hair and an unconvincing mustache gestured toward an alley.

events.speaker: BLOND YOUTH
events.text: He's right down there.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel followed. She was weak, but surely she could heal one person.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Several people surrounded her in the alley, some carrying crude blades.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: Bet you have money, so cough it up.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel didn't know what money was. Their emotions—fear, worry, anger and envy—blurred together.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Why don't we talk?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Her gestures only confused them. One youth waved a knife so wildly that he nearly cut his friend's ear.

events.speaker: THUG
events.text: Money. Now.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel could neither outrun nor overpower them in her weakened condition.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Oi, you lil' rats causing trouble again?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A broad man approached with a hammer, his leather apron damp with sweat.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: Buzz off, pops. We don't need a geezer interfering with our business.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: It's my business when you're doing it in the town my children were raised in.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The youth mouthed something that angered Alric. He punched the boy, who landed flat on his rear.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: You did it now, Alric.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Two thugs stood watch over Haniel as the others surrounded Alric.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric knocked several attackers down, but one drove a knife into his shoulder. The smith roared and fell to one knee.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Little bastards...

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: Just shut up and die already.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The youth tossed his knife and caught it, his nose still bloody. Then a shadow appeared behind him.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus lifted the leader by the back of his head. Haniel sensed malice and bloodlust—but beneath it, something protective.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: What the hell?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus pulled the leader into a knife's path as a shield, then kicked him into the attacker. The remaining thugs fled.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: Who even are you? Are you her husband or something?!

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Asmodeus.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He didn't look her way. The boy tried to flee, but Asmodeus knocked him down and planted a foot on his back.

events.speaker: GANG LEADER
events.text: Get off me, psycho!

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Asmodeus.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel hurried forward, but Asmodeus grasped the boy's wrist. A sickening crunch followed.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel reached to heal the sobbing youth. Alric placed a strong hand on her shoulder.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I understand you want to aid him, but you should let him learn his lesson.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She felt no hatred from Alric, only cool calmness. Tears ran down her face, but she listened.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I'll call his folks. They were too soft on him when he was a boy, so I'm sure they will mend him.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric sat the youth against the alley wall, and Asmodeus returned to Haniel.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She wondered whether what she had witnessed was the dual nature of humankind—and, looking at Asmodeus, the nature of a demon.
